title: Food Science & Functions: Stretch
welcome_lead: Stretch into the working chemistry of bread, foams and gels.
meta_desc: Stretch GCSE food science: gluten development, foams, gels, syneresis, enzymes.
final_note: Once you understand the chemistry, recipes become predictable.

walkthroughs.body_html: Two wheat proteins, gliadin and glutenin, combine with water to form gluten. Kneading aligns and strengthens the network, trapping the carbon dioxide produced by yeast so the dough rises and holds its shape.

A whipped egg-white meringue is a foam — air trapped in a protein liquid that then sets in the oven. A jelly is a gel — gelatin or pectin forming a network that traps water. Over time, water can seep out: syneresis.

When you cut an apple, enzymes inside its cells react with oxygen, producing brown pigments — enzymic browning. Slow it with acid (lemon juice), cold (fridge) or by blanching, which denatures the enzymes.
